safety_lead_time.comparison_action: Reduce SAP safety lead time from 3.0 to 1.5 days

narrative: Material PL2__MCB48083 exhibits stable, high-volume daily demand (~116K units/day, CV=0.20) with no detectable trend across the 131-day observation window. Lead times average 1.56 working days but show moderate variability (CV=0.60), occasionally spiking to ~4.8 days. The current SAP policy carries zero safety stock, which is insufficient to maintain the 95% service-level target given this lead-time variability. An (r,Q) continuous-review policy with a safety stock of 184,159 units and an EOQ-derived order quantity of 591,311 units is recommended, reducing total annual inventory cost by over 95% while satisfying the storage capacity constraint.
warnings: Order quantity capped from unconstrained EOQ 775,470 to 591,311 due to storage capacity constraint of 843,693 units with safety stock of 184,159 units.
Two low-demand outliers detected (values ~23K and ~57K); winsorisation applied at 1st/99th percentile.

research_insights.selection_rationale: Stable, continuously-positive, high-volume demand with moderate lead-time variability is textbook territory for a continuous-review (r,Q) policy. The EOQ minimises the sum of ordering and holding costs; the reorder point r = mean_LTD + safety_stock ensures the 95% service level is met even under lead-time spikes.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity of 843,693 units binds the unconstrained EOQ (775,470 + 184,159 = 959,629 > 843,693). The order quantity was reduced to 591,311 units to respect this hard limit. This increases ordering frequency slightly (~25 orders/year vs ~19 unconstrained) but remains economically sound. Service level is unaffected as safety stock is preserved.
